levels.name: Somport tunnels and underground laboratory
levels.note: Plan view. Houses the Somport road tunnel (geometry:canfranc-tunnel-somport-road), the partially-mapped historic rail tunnel (geometry:canfranc-tunnel-rail-somport-stub) and the laboratory itself (geometry:canfranc-lab-underground), between them under Mount Tobazo.

name: LSC — Laboratorio Subterráneo de Canfranc
notes: The site coordinate of site:lsc-canfranc used to be the same OSM feature as geometry:canfranc-surface-building (42.7493154, -0.5162702, precision_m 500), the laboratory's administrative offices at Canfranc-Estación, about 3.0 km from the underground laboratory itself (geometry:canfranc-lab-underground, an independently OSM-tagged feature 'Galería de evacuación 12', Aía); it has been replaced by the point of geometry:canfranc-lab-underground.

The historic Canfranc railway tunnel is only partially traced in OpenStreetMap (about 1.28 km of a tunnel usually cited at ~7.8 km); geometry:canfranc-tunnel-rail-somport-stub is drawn as a partial trace rather than extended by guesswork. A fuller OpenStreetMap trace or a surveyed tunnel plan would allow the whole tunnel to be drawn.

summary.plain: The Canfranc Underground Laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees: a laboratory dug beneath Mount Tobazo between the historic (1928) railway tunnel and the modern (2003) Somport road tunnel, under about 800 metres of rock.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory. The Somport road tunnel (OSM ways 29050143 + 76450688 + 1356486837, length-checked at 0.34% against a civil-engineering journal article) is drawn as context, alongside a partial trace of the historic rail tunnel. The laboratory itself is a separately OSM-tagged feature (way 1075274236) about 3.0 km from the surface administrative building at Canfranc-Estación (way 711426145).
